full_judgment: 5. But we do not think that this ground, which the learned Advocated has agitated, is at all sufficient for review of the judgment in question. This review petitioner, being defendant, contested in all the three courts below, but he did not raise this question before any of those courts. It further appears that though the boundaries of the land contracted to be sold, as stated in alleged bainapatra, and the boundaries of the suit land, as stated in the schedule to the plaint show some dissimilarities, the khatian number and plot number etc. stated in the 'bainapatra' and in the scheduled to the plaint are same. Where all the courts and also this court have found the alleged contract for sale genuine and where the defendant review-petitioner does not have any reason to assail these concurrent findings and decision of all the courts as to genuineness of the bainapatra in question we do not think that the only ground which has been agitated in this review petition is sufficient at all to review the judgment and order in question. The defendant-petitioner got ample opportunity to agitate this ground before the courts below and also before this Division at the time of hearing of civil petition for leave to appeal, but he did not do so.
